identity.what_it_is: NYC Parks' public Atlantic beach and Riegelmann Boardwalk in Coney Island, Brooklyn; Parks lists it together with Brighton Beach as 'Coney Island and Brighton Beach'.
identity.where: Brooklyn, on the Atlantic Ocean, from W. 37th Street to Ocean Parkway (Parks beach page).
identity.warnings: Parks manages Coney Island and Brighton Beach as one listing; Manhattan Beach is a separate Parks beach with its own rules. The Manhattan Beach rules in the bundle are NOT Coney rules. Pages on nyc.gov were captured at the end of the 2026 season, so 'open now' wording is stale (beaches closed until Memorial Day weekend 2027).

spike_candidates.statement: On July 6, 2026 Coney Island's water tested at 227 enterococci per 100 mL, over double the 104 limit, and reporters found one small boardwalk sign.
spike_candidates.tension: The city says swimming is not recommended, yet people on the sand were still entering the water with little on-site warning; the beach stays open, only swimming is advised against.

spike_candidates.statement: Two teenage sisters vanished in the water off Coney Island shortly after 8 p.m. on July 5, 2024, two hours after lifeguards left at 6 p.m.
spike_candidates.tension: The beach and boardwalk run 24 hours with Parks staff on site, but swimming is only guarded from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., and red-flag warnings were already posted.

spike_candidates.statement: Coney Island is the only NYC beach with a 24-hour Parks operation, but the water is lifeguarded only 8 hours a day.
spike_candidates.tension: A Parks commissioner calls it the safest feeling place at night, while every recent local drowning story hinges on the hours when lifeguards are off.

spike_candidates.statement: The F/Q West 8th Street-NY Aquarium stop is the southernmost station in the whole NYC subway, and its 700-foot aquarium bridge was torn down in 2013.
spike_candidates.tension: The closest-to-the-sea stop carries only about a fifth of Stillwell Avenue's riders (679,646 vs 3,475,833 in 2024) and lost its direct pedestrian link to the aquarium.

spike_candidates.statement: In September 2025 a 4-2 panel vote, with 921 written comments against and 17 for, killed a $3 billion Thor Equities casino beside the Coney Island boardwalk.
spike_candidates.tension: Residents who asked for lifeguards and teachers, not blackjack, beat a developer who promised $200 million and thousands of jobs, and the state's three licenses then went to Queens and the Bronx.

spike_candidates.statement: The Cyclone, now headed for its 100th birthday in 2027, was bought by the city in 1969 and nearly replaced in 1972 with an aquarium swamp display.
spike_candidates.tension: A landmark now sold as timeless was saved only because the city could not find a better use and Astroland bid $57,000 a year in 1975.

spike_candidates.statement: The Parachute Jump, built for the 1939 World's Fair and lit by about 8,000 fixtures, is the only part of Steeplechase Park left; Fred Trump bought the site in 1965 and wanted the tower sold for scrap.
spike_candidates.tension: The skyline symbol of Coney Island was a scrap-metal liability nobody wanted, and even its closing year (1964 or 1968) is still disputed.

spike_candidates.statement: The Mermaid Parade ends at 4 p.m. with the king and queen leading a procession to the beach at 19th Street to officially open the summer swimming season.
spike_candidates.tension: The 'start of summer' is a costume ritual at the water's edge, and in 2026 the parade nearly died for lack of money before the community raised it back.

spike_candidates.statement: In 1904 the public had about 1.4 square inches of Coney Island beachfront per New Yorker, and a 1913 court ruling gave the beach back to the state.
spike_candidates.tension: The famous free people's beach was private, fenced and sold off until courts and a 1921 land taking reopened it.

spike_candidates.statement: Nobody paid at the sand: in the Depression Luna Park admitted it could not compete with a beach that charged no admission.
spike_candidates.tension: The free beach and the five-cent subway, not the rides, were what the poor of New York actually bought.

spike_candidates.statement: On 29 July 1907 Steeplechase burned and George Tilyou posted a sign selling admission to the burning ruins for ten cents.
spike_candidates.tension: The fire cleared 35 acres and the owner turned the disaster into a ticket sale the next morning.

spike_candidates.statement: In 1946 Steeplechase's pool used a pass scheme that locked out African Americans while Black visitors were a growing share of the park.
spike_candidates.tension: The 'everyone's playground' story had a quiet color line, and no source in this bundle documents the beach itself.

spike_candidates.statement: From 1903 to 1943 a doctor who probably was not a doctor kept premature babies alive in a 25-cent Luna Park sideshow.
spike_candidates.tension: Mainstream medicine rejected incubators, so premature infants were saved by an amusement-park ticket window.

spike_candidates.statement: In 1965-66 Fred Trump bought Steeplechase Park, never reopened it, held a brick-throwing demolition party and bulldozed it before it could be landmarked.
spike_candidates.tension: The loss of one park created a worldwide impression that all of Coney Island had closed, and Trump never built the housing he wanted.

spike_candidates.statement: After Hurricane Sandy the beach lost about 600,000 cubic yards of sand, but the flooding that hurt people most came from Coney Island Creek, not the ocean.
spike_candidates.tension: Rebuilt sand dunes saved an estimated $494 million, yet the creek that flooded homes is toxic and still has no cleanup plan.

spike_candidates.statement: A draft $52 billion Army Corps plan would raise the boardwalk five feet with a concrete barrier covering about a third of it, with construction starting around 2030.
spike_candidates.tension: Protecting the beach from storms could wall off ocean views and change the boardwalk the city fought over in 2012.

spike_candidates.statement: In 2012 the city's design commission voted 6-0 to replace part of the 1923 wooden boardwalk with concrete and recycled plastic lumber.
spike_candidates.tension: Residents who said it would turn a boardwalk into a sidewalk lost in the review process and, per CBS 2014, in court.

spike_candidates.statement: Nathan's July 4 hot dog contest 'since 1916' was invented: promoter Mortimer Matz admitted in 2010 he made it up in the early 1970s.
spike_candidates.tension: The company's own history page still prints the 1916 contest as 'legend has it' while its first recorded contest is 1972 and the first official one was 1967.

spike_candidates.statement: A $30,000 film shot on Coney Island in 1953, Little Fugitive, made a 7-year-old with $6 the template for the French New Wave, per Truffaut.
spike_candidates.tension: The Coney Island it records, safe enough for a child alone, is the one the 1979 Warriors shows as shuttered and gone to seed.

spike_candidates.statement: Ruby's, open since 1934, was ordered out in November 2010 after the city paid $100 million for the amusement zone.
spike_candidates.tension: The street beside the bar is co-named for its owner, yet the city's own land deal started the eviction; no source here says whether the bar reopened.

spike_candidates.statement: The Warriors, the most famous Coney Island film, never filmed in the Bronx, and commenters say its beach ending was shot at Breezy Point or Fort Tilden.
spike_candidates.tension: The 'Coney Island' ending that fans quote may not be Coney Island, and the best proof is a reader comment, not an official source.

spike_candidates.statement: Of the three named Coney boardwalk restrooms, only the Brighton 1 Rd-2 St one is listed wheelchair accessible and it lists no changing tables; W 27 St and W 33 St list one table per room.
spike_candidates.tension: A parent or wheelchair user cannot tell from the city pages which restroom serves both needs.

spike_candidates.statement: The West 27th Street women's room failed its structural check on June 13, 2025, while the park as a whole scores 87.
spike_candidates.tension: The city's own inspection page shows a failing item while the park overall scores 87.

spike_candidates.statement: In 2019 the Comptroller found 73% of NYC park comfort stations had no baby-changing station and only 31% were ADA accessible; Coney's 2025 dataset lists 6 of 8 zones with changing stations.
spike_candidates.tension: Coney's beach restroom zones look better than the citywide 2019 picture, but only 2 of 8 zones are year-round.

facts.quote: bmt brighton line ind culver line bmt sea beach line bmt west end line

facts.fact: Stillwell is an elevated station at 1243 Surf Avenue with four island platforms and eight tracks.
facts.quote: platforms 4 island platforms tracks 8

facts.fact: Stillwell's lines opened in stages from September 5, 1917 (Sea Beach) to May 1, 1920 (Culver), and the terminal was rebuilt and reopened May 29, 2005.
facts.quote: rebuilt may 29, 2005

facts.fact: Stillwell had 3,475,833 subway riders in 2024.
Buses serving Stillwell are B36, B64, B68, B74, B82, X28 and X38; the station is listed as accessible.
facts.quote: nyct bus: b36, b64, b68, b74, b82, x28, x38

facts.fact: West Eighth Street-NY Aquarium is the southernmost station in the whole NYC subway system.
facts.quote: this station is geographically the southernmost station in the entire new york city subway system.
facts.source_title: Wikipedia - West Eighth Street-New York Aquarium station

facts.fact: F and Q trains stop at W 8th St at all times, with an extra F during peak rush hours.
facts.quote: it is served by the f and q trains at all times, and by the < f > train during rush hours in the peak direction.
facts.source_title: Wikipedia - West Eighth Street-New York Aquarium station

facts.fact: W 8th St had 679,646 riders in 2024, about a fifth of Stillwell's volume.
facts.source_title: Wikipedia - West Eighth Street-New York Aquarium station

facts.fact: The W 8th St station opened May 19, 1919; Brighton trains began serving it June 13, 1919.
facts.quote: opened may 19, 1919
facts.source_title: Wikipedia - West Eighth Street-New York Aquarium station

facts.fact: In 1954 the transit authority announced a 700-foot overpass to the planned aquarium, with an estimated cost of $500,000 and completion by November 1955.
facts.quote: the estimated cost for the project was $500,000, and it was expected to be completed by november 1955.
facts.source_title: Wikipedia - West Eighth Street-New York Aquarium station

facts.fact: The station closed August 2002 and reopened May 23, 2004 during the Stillwell rebuild.
facts.quote: the station was closed in august 2002 in conjunction with the reconstruction of the coney island-stillwell avenue terminal, and service was restored on may 23, 2004.
facts.source_title: Wikipedia - West Eighth Street-New York Aquarium station

facts.fact: The pedestrian bridge to the aquarium was torn down August 8, 2013 for safety reasons and replaced by a crosswalk and wider sidewalks.
facts.quote: the pedestrian bridge was torn down on august 8, 2013, due to safety issues.
facts.source_title: Wikipedia - West Eighth Street-New York Aquarium station

facts.fact: The W 8th St station has a 2005 artwork called Wavewall by Vito Acconci.
facts.quote: the 2005 artwork here is called wavewall by vito acconci.
facts.source_title: Wikipedia - West Eighth Street-New York Aquarium station

facts.fact: The Aquarium (602 Surf Ave) says take F or Q to W 8th St, or N/D to Stillwell then walk two blocks east on Surf.
facts.quote: take the f or q train to the west 8th street station on coney island, brooklyn. alternatively, take the n or d trains to the coney island-stillwell avenue station, then walk two blocks east on surf ave.

facts.fact: The B36 stops at Surf Ave and W 8th St, and the B68 at Neptune Ave and W 8th St.
facts.quote: take the b36 to surf ave. and west 8th st. or take the b68 to neptune ave. and west 8th st.

facts.fact: In summer, Surf Avenue traffic is regulated so cars can only turn left into the aquarium lot, approaching westbound from Ocean Parkway.
facts.quote: during the busy summer season, traffic on surf avenue is regulated to only allow for a left turn into the aquarium parking lot.

facts.fact: Driving from Manhattan: Brooklyn-Battery Tunnel, BQE west, exit 22 to Belt Pkwy east, exit 7 (Ocean Pkwy) to Surf Ave.
facts.quote: take exit 22 to the belt pkwy east.

facts.fact: From Long Island and Queens take the Belt Parkway west to exit 7B and Ocean Parkway to Surf Avenue.
facts.quote: take the belt pkwy west to exit 7b (ocean pkwy).

facts.fact: From Staten Island, the Verrazzano route uses exit 7S to Ocean Parkway south.
facts.quote: to belt pkwy east to exit 7s (ocean pkwy south).

facts.fact: Deno's Wonder Wheel sits on the boardwalk between the original Nathan's and the New York Aquarium.
facts.quote: between the original nathan's famous hot dog restaurant and the new york aquarium.

facts.fact: Deno's directions from Stillwell: head toward the beach, climb to the boardwalk, turn left and walk one block.
facts.quote: when you get up to the boardwalk, turn left and walk one block.

facts.fact: Deno's site gives the 2026 park opening as April 12 with kiddie rides at 11 a.m. and adult rides at noon.
facts.quote: park opens april 12. kiddie park opens at 11am and adult rides open at noon.

facts.fact: The street was renamed Denos Vourderis Place (formerly W. 12th St.), Deno's phone is 718 372 2592.
facts.quote: denos vourderis place (formerly w. 12th st.)

facts.fact: Rip-current guidance from the National Weather Service is linked from Parks' beach page.
facts.quote: rip currents - safety tips and information provided by the national weather service regarding the dangers of rip currents.
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Coney Island and Brighton Beach

facts.fact: Sick after swimming? The Health Department says seek care and report it to 311.
facts.quote: if you suspect you got sick after swimming at a beach, seek medical attention promptly and report your illness by calling 311.

facts.fact: Even when swimming is banned, walking, running and sitting on the sand and boardwalk are allowed during regular park hours.
facts.quote: even when swimming and wading is not permitted, exercise such as walking and running, and spending time on the sand and boardwalk, are permitted during regular park hours.

facts.fact: Parks lets you sign up for Notify NYC beach notifications for real-time openings and closings.
facts.quote: to receive real-time opening and closing notifications

facts.fact: An advisory notice reads that swimming and wading are not recommended and directs people to 311 or nyc.gov/notifynyc.
facts.quote: one or more new york city area beaches are currently under an advisory.
facts.source_title: NYC Emergency Management - Notify NYC beach advisory

facts.fact: The DOH data portal says each beach is sampled every week and Rockaway/Breezy Point twice each week.
facts.quote: each beach is monitored and sampled every week, except for rockaway and breezy point beaches, which are sampled twice each week.
facts.source_title: NYC EH Data Portal - Beach water quality

facts.fact: Each bathing beach needs a Health Department permit and is inspected for compliance during the swim season.
facts.quote: a permit is required from the nyc health department for each bathing beach and its facilities.

facts.fact: Deno's Wonder Wheel is a 150-foot eccentric Ferris wheel at Deno's Wonder Wheel Amusement Park, where some cabins slide on rails instead of staying fixed to the rim.
facts.quote: the wonder wheel is a 150-foot-tall (46 m) eccentric ferris wheel at deno's wonder wheel amusement park at coney island

facts.fact: The Wonder Wheel first opened on Memorial Day 1920 (Wikipedia infobox gives May 30, 1920).
facts.quote: the wheel first opened on memorial day in 1920.

facts.fact: Sixteen of the 24 cabins slide inward on winding tracks as the wheel turns; the other eight are fixed to the rim for a traditional Ferris wheel ride, with separate queues for each.
facts.quote: sixteen of the cars slide inward on snaking tracks, falling outward as the wheel rotates.

facts.fact: One rotation takes ten minutes and the ride makes two rotations; hourly capacity is 864 riders.
facts.quote: each rotation of the wheel takes ten minutes, giving the ride a total hourly capacity of 864.

facts.fact: The Wonder Wheel's all-time one-day record is 14,506 passengers on July 4, 1947.
facts.quote: the ride set an all-time daily ridership record on july 4, 1947, when it carried 14,506 passengers.

facts.fact: Denos Vourderis bought the wheel from Fred Garms and his cousin Walter Kerner Sr. on June 7, 1983, for $250,000; Atlas Obscura gives the same date and price.
facts.quote: on june 7, 1983, vourderis bought the wonder wheel from garms and his cousin walter kerner sr.

facts.fact: The only handover instructions the Vourderis family got were two words, 'good luck', scribbled on a cardboard cigarette box (Atlas Obscura says on the back of a cigarette carton).
facts.quote: the only maintenance instructions given to the vourderis family were the words

facts.fact: The Wonder Wheel is New York City Landmark no. 1708, designated May 23, 1989.
facts.quote: new york city landmark designated may 23, 1989 reference no. 1708

facts.fact: Atlas Obscura says the wheel was put on the National Register of Historic Places in 1984 and made a city landmark five years later; Wikipedia's wheel page gives no NRHP date.
facts.quote: the wonder wheel was listed on the national register of historic places in 1984

facts.fact: As of 2018 the wheel had given more than 35 million rides; Atlas Obscura (2016) also says over 35 million.
facts.quote: as of 2018 [ update ], over 35 million rides had been taken on the wheel since it first opened.

facts.fact: A Wonder Wheel ride costs 10 credits, and the per-credit price drops with larger purchases; the Wikipedia article gives no dollar figure.
facts.quote: a ride on the wonder wheel costs 10 credits; the cost of each credit varies depending on how many are purchased.

facts.fact: Wikipedia calls the Wonder Wheel the oldest continuous operating ride at Coney Island as of 2024.
facts.quote: the wonder wheel is the oldest continuous operating ride at coney island

facts.fact: The wheel did not run at all in 2020 (COVID), the first lost season in its history, and reopened in April 2021, so 'continuous' is not literally true.
facts.quote: the 2020 season was the first in which the wonder wheel did not operate at all

facts.fact: The only time the wheel stopped on its own was the July 13, 1977 citywide blackout, when the owners hand-cranked it to unload riders.
facts.quote: the only time the wheel stopped while not under the control of the operator was during the new york city blackout on july 13, 1977.

facts.fact: Hurricane Sandy flooded Deno's park in 2012 but the wheel was only slightly damaged and reopened the next year.
facts.quote: even during the aftermath of 2012's hurricane sandy, when deno's amusement park was flooded, the wonder wheel was only slightly damaged and reopened the next year.

facts.fact: Deno's is called the last family-operated amusement park in Coney Island, and the family has refused offers to sell.
facts.quote: deno's wonder wheel amusement park is the last family-operated amusement park in coney island

facts.fact: The wheel is nicknamed the most romantic ride in the world and is a common spot for proposals and newlywed rides.
facts.quote: the most romantic ride in the world

facts.fact: Deno Vourderis was born in Aigion, Greece, in 1920, the eighth of 22 children, came to the US at 14 and first sold hot dogs from a Manhattan pushcart.
facts.quote: was born in aigion, greece in 1920. he was the eighth of 22 children.

facts.fact: Wheel tickets jumped from 50 cents in 1976 to $1.25 in 1981.
facts.quote: the wonder wheel raised ticket prices significantly, from $0.50 in 1976 to $1.25 by 1981.

facts.fact: In the 1960s-70s two German shepherds guarded the wheel and nearby rides at night, and rode in a cabin by day.
facts.quote: the wheel and surrounding attractions were protected by two german shepherds at night

facts.fact: The wheel's address is 3059 West 12th Street, just north of the boardwalk (Atlas Obscura lists 3048 Jones Walk).
facts.quote: the wonder wheel is located at 3059 west 12th street, just north of the riegelmann boardwalk.

facts.fact: Atlas Obscura describes the wheel as seasonal, roughly Easter to Halloween, weekends first and daily from Memorial Day; this is a 2016 description and needs a current check.
facts.quote: the wonder wheel is a seasonal ride which operates roughly between easter and halloween.

facts.fact: The Parachute Jump is a 250-foot, 170-ton open steel tower with twelve arms, now a defunct ride.
facts.quote: the structure consists of a 250-foot-tall (76 m), 170-short-ton (150 t) open-frame, steel parachute tower.

facts.fact: The Life Savers Parachute Jump opened at the 1939 New York World's Fair on May 27, 1939; the pole-topped tower reached 262 feet there.
facts.quote: the life savers parachute jump opened on may 27, 1939

facts.fact: At the 1939 fair a Parachute Jump ride cost 40 cents for adults and 25 cents for children.
facts.quote: each ride cost $0.40 (equivalent to $9.26 in 2025) for adults and $0.25 (equivalent to $5.79 in 2025) for children.

facts.fact: The Tilyou family, owners of Steeplechase Park, bought the jump for $150,000 and rebuilt it on the boardwalk in 1941; it reopened in May 1941.
facts.quote: frank tilyou and george tilyou jr., the owners of steeplechase park, acquired the jump for $150,000

facts.fact: At Steeplechase the jump drew up to half a million riders each season, most going up in just under a minute and dropping in 11 to 15 seconds.
facts.quote: the parachute jump attracted up to half a million riders during each annual operating season.

facts.fact: Steeplechase Park closed for good on September 20, 1964, and the next year the property was sold to developer Fred Trump.
facts.quote: on september 20, 1964, steeplechase park closed for the last time, and the next year, the property was sold to developer fred trump.

facts.fact: Historian Charles Denson and the Coney Island History Project say the jump closed in 1964 and that 1968 is a repeated error.
facts.quote: the coney island historian charles denson explained that the jump closed in 1964 but that many publications give an erroneous date of 1968.

facts.fact: NYC Parks' website and engineer Helen Harrison still say the jump closed in 1968; Harrison says the last documented incident was May 30, 1968.
facts.quote: consulting engineer helen harrison and the new york city department of parks and recreation 's website also cite a closure date of 1968

facts.fact: A third closing date appears: the Brooklyn Paper says the jump was shuttered in 1965, and a 1965 Daily News article said it had been stripped of wires and chutes.
facts.quote: while the brooklyn paper says the jump was shuttered in 1965.

facts.fact: In 1966 the Coney Island Chamber of Commerce asked the Landmarks Commission to protect the jump, but Fred Trump wanted to sell it as scrap and said it was too young to be a landmark.
facts.quote: trump, however, wanted to sell it as scrap and did not think it was old enough to warrant landmark status.

facts.fact: In 1968 the city voted to buy the Steeplechase site for $4 million; NYC Parks then tried to auction the jump in 1971 and got no bids.
facts.quote: the city voted in 1968 to acquire the site for $4 million

facts.fact: Parachute Jump designations: National Register Sept 2, 1980; state register Oct 23, 1981; NYC Landmark no. 1638 on May 23, 1989 (the same day as the Wonder Wheel).
facts.quote: significant dates added to nrhp september 2, 1980 designated nysrhp october 23, 1981 designated nycl may 23, 1989

facts.fact: The tower's light system was switched on in 2006 and replaced in 2013; it has been lit in memory of events such as Kobe Bryant's death.
facts.quote: the lights were activated in 2006 and replaced in a subsequent project in 2013.

facts.fact: The frame carries about 8,000 lighting fixtures for night light shows.
facts.quote: the frame has about 8,000 lighting fixtures, which are used for night-time light shows.

facts.fact: The Parachute Jump stands on the boardwalk between West 16th and West 19th Streets, in Steeplechase Plaza.
facts.quote: the parachute jump is on the riegelmann boardwalk at coney island between west 16th and west 19th streets.

facts.fact: The current Luna Park opened May 29, 2010 on the site of Astroland (1962-2008) and the one-season Dreamland carnival of 2009.
facts.quote: it opened on may 29, 2010, at the site of astroland

facts.fact: Mayor Bloomberg announced on Feb 16, 2010 that Zamperla/Central Amusement International won a 10-year lease on the 3.16-acre Astroland site; what has happened since that lease would have ended in 2020 is not in these sources.
facts.quote: would be awarded to zamperla/central amusement international under a 10-year lease.

facts.fact: On July 2, 2013 Luna Park was evacuated when the leftover Astroland Astrotower began swaying; it was demolished by July 6.
facts.quote: on july 2, 2013, luna park was evacuated as a precaution due to a problem with the astrotower swaying

facts.fact: A 2018 city plan to add a log flume, zip line and ropes course would enlarge Luna Park by 50 percent and add 100 jobs; construction began October 2021.
facts.quote: the expansion would enlarge the park by 50 percent and were expected to add 100 jobs.

facts.fact: Four of the new expansion rides opened in June 2023, including the Tony's Express coaster and Leti's Treasure log flume.
facts.quote: four of the new rides opened in june 2023.

facts.fact: Wikipedia says Luna Park does not accept cash for rides; visitors must use cards or credits or an unlimited wristband.
facts.quote: it is the only area on coney island where the use of cash to pay for amusements and rides is not allowed

facts.fact: Wikipedia says the unlimited wristband gives four hours of ride time on select rides.
facts.quote: an unlimited ride wristband that allows four hours of ride time on select rides.

facts.fact: Luna Park's own homepage banner sells an all-day wristband: all rides, all day, one price, with no price shown in the text.
facts.quote: all rides. all day. one price. purchase the all day wristband now!
facts.source_title: Luna Park in Coney Island (official site)

facts.fact: Wikipedia says Luna Park has 36 Zamperla-made attractions, but the same article says 19 new attractions at opening and a infobox total of 28; counts differ inside the page.
facts.quote: luna park has 36 attractions designed and manufactured by zamperla.

facts.fact: Luna Park's 2026 season opened Saturday March 28 at 11 a.m.; the egg-cream christening of the Cyclone was Sunday March 29.
facts.quote: the seaside institution will reopen this saturday, march 28 at 11am

facts.fact: Park entry is free and rides start at $4 (2026 season).
facts.quote: admission remains free, with rides starting at $4

facts.fact: Time Out says Luna Park is open daily in spring break (April 2 to 12), Fri-Sun until Memorial Day, then daily.
facts.quote: luna park will be open daily during spring break (april 2 to 12) and every friday, saturday and sunday until memorial day.

facts.fact: Luna Park's own homepage lists spring break daily opening as April 11th through 20th, which differs from the press dates; the page is undated.
facts.quote: we're open daily for spring break! april 11th through 20th!
facts.source_title: Luna Park in Coney Island (official site)

facts.fact: Luna Park's homepage advertises a Luna Pass starting from $40.
facts.quote: luna pass starting from $40
facts.source_title: Luna Park in Coney Island (official site)

facts.fact: Luna Park's official address is 1000 Surf Avenue, Brooklyn 11224; phone 718-373-5862.
facts.quote: luna park in coney island 1000 surf avenue brooklyn, ny 11224
facts.source_title: Luna Park in Coney Island (official site)

facts.fact: Alessandro Zamperla is president and CEO of Central Amusement International, which runs Luna Park, and spoke at the 2026 opening.
facts.quote: it is an honor to continue the incomparable amusement legacy in coney island

facts.fact: Each opening weekend the first riders get a free Cyclone ride and egg cream, one for each year of age; in 2026 it was 99, starting a countdown to the 2027 centennial.
facts.quote: the first 99 riders on sunday will score a free spin on the iconic coaster and a classic egg cream (while supplies last).

facts.fact: In winter 2023 Luna Park stayed open for the first time in its history for Frost Fest (Nov 18 to Jan 7) with an ice rink; no source here says if it repeated.
facts.quote: luna park in coney island will stay open this winter for the first time in its 120-year history
facts.source_title: 6sqft Mermaid Parade page with related stories

facts.fact: For 2026 Luna Park refreshed midway games, retail spots and food options.
facts.quote: you'll find some updated midway and arcade games, refreshed retail spots and a few new food options

facts.fact: The Cyclone, designed by Vernon Keenan, opened June 26, 1927.
facts.quote: designed by vernon keenan, it opened to the public on june 26, 1927.

facts.fact: A Cyclone ride cost 25 cents in 1927 (35 cents Sundays and holidays); the ride was built for a reported $146,000 to $175,000.
facts.quote: when the cyclone opened on june 26, 1927, a ride cost 25 cents

facts.fact: Wikipedia's infobox gives New York City Landmark no. 1636 designated June 12, 1988, but its own reference lists the LPC report as dated July 12, 1988; NRHP listing June 25, 1991 (state register June 13, 1991).
facts.quote: new york city landmark designated june 12, 1988 reference no. 1636

facts.fact: The Cyclone's height is 75 feet; the 85 feet often quoted is the measurement to the sign above the lift hill.
facts.quote: some sources cite a height of 85 ft (26 m), though the roller coaster database reports that this is the measurement to the sign above the lift hill

facts.fact: Wikipedia says a Cyclone ride lasts about one minute 50 seconds (its infobox says 2:30; NYC Tourism says 2 minutes).
facts.quote: each ride takes about one minute and fifty seconds

facts.fact: Luna Park's own page calls the Cyclone the second-steepest wooden coaster in the world with an 85-foot plunge; Wikipedia ranks its drop ninth-steepest as of 2014.
facts.quote: as the second-steepest wooden roller coaster in the world

facts.fact: Each Cyclone train seats 24, two across in four rows, with lap bars and no headrests; only one of three trains runs at a time.
facts.quote: riders are arranged two across in four rows, for a total of 24 riders per train.

facts.fact: The Cyclone height requirement is 54 inches (Thunderbolt is 50 inches).
facts.quote: height restriction 54 in (137 cm)

facts.fact: The city bought the Cyclone for $1.2 million in 1969 and the ride soon racked up 101 safety violations.
facts.quote: the city bought the cyclone for $1.2 million in 1969.

facts.fact: In 1972 New York Aquarium officials announced they would replace the Cyclone with a swamp display, which triggered a Save the Cyclone campaign.
facts.quote: in 1972, aquarium officials announced that they would replace the cyclone with a swamp display.

facts.fact: Astroland won the 1975 lease at $57,000 a year, spent $60,000 on repairs, and reopened the Cyclone on July 3, 1975.
facts.quote: the owners of the astroland amusement park won the lease, with a bid of $57,000 per year.

facts.fact: Luna Park took over the Cyclone in 2011 (after Astroland closed in 2008) and Great Coasters International finished a refurbishment in 2016.
facts.quote: the adjacent luna park took over management of the cyclone in 2011

facts.fact: At least three people have died after riding the Cyclone (1985, 1988, 2007); the 1985 and 1988 victims stood up during the ride.
facts.quote: at least three people have died after riding the cyclone.

facts.fact: On Aug 22, 2024 the Cyclone stopped mid-ride after a cracked lift-chain sprocket was found; riders were evacuated unhurt, the city cited Luna Park for two violations and the ride reopened Sept 7.
facts.quote: on august 22, 2024, the cyclone was halted mid-ride upon discovery of a crack in the lift hill chain's sprocket

facts.fact: Charles Lindbergh was said to have ridden the Cyclone two years after it opened and called it greater than flying an airplane at top speed (reported, not confirmed).
facts.quote: aviator charles lindbergh was said to have ridden the cyclone two years after it opened

facts.fact: In 1948 the New York Times reported a mute man, Emilio Franco, got his voice back on the Cyclone; his first words were I feel sick.
facts.quote: regained his voice after riding the cyclone

facts.fact: In 1977 19-year-old Richard Rodriguez rode the Cyclone for 104 hours straight, eating hot dogs and M&Ms between rides.
facts.quote: nineteen-year-old richard rodriguez broke the record from august 18 to 22, 1977, riding the coaster for 104 hours.

facts.fact: The Cyclone inspired the name of the Brooklyn Cyclones minor league baseball team.
facts.quote: it inspired the name of the brooklyn cyclones baseball team

facts.fact: Timber-supported coasters can no longer be built under modern New York City building codes, so the Cyclone cannot be rebuilt.
facts.quote: since timber-supported coasters can no longer be built under modern new york city building codes

facts.fact: NYC Tourism writers said the Cyclone's neon sign, shaky platform and bumpy ride make you feel like the Coolidge administration never ended.
facts.quote: the cyclone's vintage neon signage, shaky waiting platform and bumpy ride make you feel like the coolidge administration never ended

facts.fact: Bonus credits from bulk credit purchases cannot be used on the Cyclone, per Wikipedia.
facts.quote: accumulated by the purchase of ride credits cannot be used for the coaster

facts.fact: The new steel Thunderbolt at Luna Park finally opened June 14, 2014, after repeated delays from Memorial Day.
facts.quote: thunderbolt finally opened on june 14, 2014.

facts.fact: Thunderbolt has 2,234 feet of track, a top speed of 56 mph, a 90-degree drop, four inversions and a $9 million cost; it is a Zamperla ride.
facts.quote: the ride features 2,234 feet (681 m) of track and runs at a top speed of 56 miles per hour (90 km/h).

facts.fact: Luna Park's own page gives Thunderbolt track as 2,233 feet; NYC Tourism lists top speed 55 mph and biggest drop 115 feet versus Wikipedia's 56 mph and 112 feet.
facts.quote: experience the 2,233 feet of steel track, twists, bends, and plunges

facts.fact: The original wooden Thunderbolt ran under George Moran from 1925 to 1982 and was torn down in 2000, so the 2014 steel coaster only borrows the name.
facts.quote: a wooden roller coaster named the thunderbolt was originally operated by george moran on coney island from 1925 to 1982.

facts.fact: Molly and George Moran, who built the original Thunderbolt, lived in a house under the coaster.
facts.quote: lived in the house underneath the roller coaster

facts.fact: Each Thunderbolt train is a single car of nine seats in three rows of three.
facts.quote: each train consists of a single car with nine seats, arranged in three rows of three.

facts.fact: Wikipedia says a Thunderbolt ride costs $12 per ride.
facts.quote: thunderbolt is a pay-per-use attraction, as guests must pay $12 for each time they ride on the coaster.

facts.fact: Luna Park's Steeplechase coaster uses saddle seats and goes 0 to 40 mph in under 2 seconds on a 1,476-foot track.
facts.quote: go 0 to 40 mph in less than 2 seconds while you giddy-up along a 1,476-foot track

facts.fact: The New York Aquarium was founded at Castle Garden in Battery Park in 1896 (opened Dec 10, 1896) and moved to Coney Island in 1957.
facts.quote: it was founded at castle garden in battery park, manhattan, in 1896, and moved to coney island in 1957.

facts.fact: Wikipedia and Architect's Newspaper both call it the oldest continually operating aquarium in the US.
facts.quote: the new york aquarium is the oldest continually operating aquarium in the united states

facts.fact: The city closed the aquarium in late 1941 and it did not reopen until 1957 at Coney Island, a 16-year gap that undercuts 'continuously operating'.
facts.quote: the city government closed the new york aquarium and moved some fish and turtles to other aquariums in late 1941.

facts.fact: The aquarium's own history page says it moved first from Castle Clinton to the Bronx Zoo and then to Coney Island in 1957; Wikipedia only says some fish stayed on view at the Bronx Zoo.
facts.quote: first from castle clinton to the bronx zoo before moving to its current home on coney island in 1957
facts.source_title: About our park - New York Aquarium

facts.fact: Castle Garden admission was free; the Coney Island aquarium charged, which the public disliked.
facts.quote: the aquarium charged admission at its coney island location; this was unpopular among members of the public

facts.fact: During Hurricane Sandy (Oct 2012) a small WCS crew stayed on site and saved 80 percent of the collection.
facts.quote: were able to save 80 percent of the animals in the collection.

facts.fact: The aquarium was fully reopened from Sandy damage in July 2022, ten years later.
facts.quote: the aquarium fully re-opened from sandy damage in july 2022.

facts.fact: Ocean Wonders: Sharks! opened to the public June 30, 2018, per Wikipedia (Architect's Newspaper gave a ribbon cutting the day before and public opening Saturday).
facts.quote: the exhibit opened on june 30, 2018

facts.fact: The $158 million Sharks addition and animal-care building cost: $111 million from New York City and $47 million from private sources.
facts.quote: of the total $158 million cost of the ocean wonders exhibit and its companion animal care facility, $111 million came from new york city and $47 million came from private groups

facts.fact: The Sharks building has 57,000 sq ft, a coral reef tunnel and a rooftop deck and shows 18 species of sharks and rays plus 115 other kinds of marine life.
facts.quote: with 18 different species of sharks and rays, plus 115 other kinds of marine life

facts.fact: The building cantilevers over the boardwalk and has an 1,100-foot kinetic wall of 33,000-plus aluminum flappers designed with artist Ned Kahn.
facts.quote: that was designed in collaboration with visual artist ned kahn to convey the force and fluidity of the ocean

facts.fact: The aquarium's own About page says it holds over 500 marine species on 14 acres; Wikipedia says 266 species.
facts.quote: the aquarium is home to over 500 species of marine wildlife
facts.source_title: About our park - New York Aquarium

facts.fact: The aquarium is at 602 Surf Avenue on 14 acres, reached by the West 8th Street-NY Aquarium subway station and the B36 bus.
facts.quote: location 602 surf avenue brooklyn, new york 11224

facts.fact: The aquarium's page says free Friday night fireworks start at 9:30 p.m.
facts.quote: the action starts at 9:30 p.m.

facts.fact: NYC Tourism says the Alliance for Coney Island's free fireworks run every Friday night in summer plus July 4, starting at 9:45 p.m.; the page is not dated and the show is over for the year.
facts.quote: the fireworks blast off at 9:45pm each of the nights.
